newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian c. bank sees further fall in yields.
newsitem.headline: Russian c. bank sees further fall in yields.

text.p: Yields on Russian government securities, which have recently hit record lows, are set to fall further this year, a senior central bank official said on Tuesday.
"They're going down and this is a firm trend," Deputy Chairman Andrei Kozlov said.
"If nothing is changed drastically by the government, this trend should continue to the end of the year," he told Reuters.
Kozlov did not give any specific rate forecasts.
The average yield on a three-month Treasury bill sold last Wednesday was 18.87 percent, the lowest ever at auction, and yields in secondary market trading have been even lower.
Yields backed up over 20 percent again on Monday.
The central bank cut its refinancing rate to 24 percent this week, the lowest since early 1992.
